about: What the smallest terminal application loads (CF1's F4; terminal design §5, the first tier: no agent endpoint): omui.size.terminal built size-optimised, as the terminal design states its tiers (§5: the workspace's `small` profile, -Oz, NDEBUG, the system's C and C++ runtimes), with its symbol table kept, the allocated sections of its program counted (.bss and the symbols left out). Bytes.

budgets.why: The terminal design's first tier (§5, D-219): 1 MB, the line of not losing to the strongest — FTXUI 334,208 B and ratatui 622,424 B for the same counter here (tests/bench/competitors/terminal). Measured 3,382,445 B (2026-11-26, GCC 16 on Linux x64, the system's C++ runtime; 3,392,536 B stripped; 4,150,490 B with libstdc++ linked in): over it, a red (terminal design §7). Its code by owner: omui.view 26%, the view's pixel parts that a terminal never draws 26% (effect shaders, raster, vector, hanim.visual, the image decoders), the standard library's instantiations 15%, text 9%, JSON and the spec's values 5%, motion 3%, the terminal host and cells 3%. Tried: -Oz, 2,705,160 B stripped with libstdc++ in, 1,938,888 B without. What brings it down, in the owners' packages: the view's pixel parts behind providers (terminal design §9 step ③), a size-optimised build (check size builds -O3), std::format and std::locale off the path (tests/size/yard's lever); tests/bench/competitors/terminal/README.md; 2026-11-27 (UI7, CF1): 2,211,981 B loaded (2,223,472 B stripped), still over it — the view's pixel parts at slots the program does not install (effects, morphs and their glyph cache, the PNG reader), a paragraph's ranges sorted by their places, the terminal's agent face a slot of its own: -1,177,429 B. Its code by owner now: omui.view 36%, the standard library's instantiations 17% (std::format's engine and its width tables about 92 KB of it), the Unicode tables 7%, text 4%, omui.core 3%, the terminal host and cells 4%, layout 3%, the frame pipeline 2.5%. At -Oz (the workspace's `web` profile) 1,221,440 B stripped. What is left: the view's own code (motion selection, presentation, undo, regions — not pixel parts), the primitives' registry (every primitive kind), std::format, and a size-optimised build that check size does not make (it builds -O3); 2026-11-27, later (CF1): measured as the design states the tier, at the workspace's `small` profile (-Oz, NDEBUG; check size builds a row at the profile it names): 1,215,758 B at 1d69ab4e's code, then only the primitives it names registered (-24,084 B), the view's motion choice and morph pass behind the morph slot (-48,560), mlibs.unicode's tables in three stages (-95,872): 1,047,242 B loaded (1,053,440 B stripped), still over it by 47,242. Its code by owner: omui.view 27.7%, the standard library's instantiations 19.4% (std::format's engine and its width and escape tables about 49 KB of it), the Unicode tables 5.1%; beside the code, the unwind tables (.eh_frame and its index 139,532 B, .gcc_except_table 19,147). What would take the rest off: openkal-linux's table of roots in .bss (10,752 B; mcpplibs/openkal-linux#61), the theme's framework motion defaults at the morph slot (about 16 KB: the motion library, the components' recipes, hanim's presences), the view's pixel effects behind a slot (about 10 KB), a presentation's projection behind the morph slot (4.4 KB), std::format off the path (about 49 KB), unwind tables only where an exception passes (-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables for this profile: mcpp applies a profile's flags to the root package's units only, measured); 2026-11-27, later (CF2's line): mlibs.json's scanner checking the grammar +80 B (1,047,322), then a presentation's projection behind the morph slot (a lease there is held and not drawn, and said once) -6,660 B: 1,040,662 B loaded, over it by 40,662

links_why: The packages built into the program (B5): a change to this list is a change to what the smallest terminal application carries, said in review. Owed: what only pixels use — mrender.raster, mrender.vector, mrender.graph, mrender.text, hanim.visual, mlibs.image and its decoders (mcpplibs.mwrap.libjpeg_turbo, .libpng, .libwebp; compat.libpng, compat.libwebp, compat.zlib), mlibs.pipeline, mlibs.rhi and the solver (mlibs.dynamics, mlibs.simulation) — reached through omui.view and hanim (terminal design §9 step ③, B6). 2026-11-27: those packages are still built in, their bytes are not (UI7: read at slots no terminal installs); the list is unchanged
